content.text:
I built `index.html`, a D3 heatmap with sensor depths as rows (2 m at the top, 40 m at the bottom) and months as columns. It renders with no errors or warnings. I checked the image after the first render. After that I made one small wording fix to the caption and rendered it again cleanly, but I did not look at the image a second time.

The main pattern: every depth has a yearly temperature cycle, and the cycle gets weaker with depth. At 2 m the warmest and coldest months differ by about 15 °C, with the warmest month in September. At 40 m they differ by only about 7 °C, and the warmest month is October. The caption is calculated from the data, not typed in.

```
REPORT
deliverable: index.html
requirements:
  R1: done - monthly mean of the daily means per depth, using d3.rollup on the loaded CSV
  R2: done - one column per month from the first date (Feb 2018) to the last (Dec 2025), year labels plus month initials
  R3: done - a month with no data for a depth is a hatched grey cell (in the legend), not filled in or set to zero
  R4: done - row labels "2 m" … "40 m", sorted shallow to deep
  R5: done - colour legend "Monthly mean water temperature (°C)"
  R6: done - title plus a one-sentence caption calculated from the data (warmest-vs-coldest month difference at the shallowest and deepest sensors, and the month each peaks)
assumptions:
  - Monthly mean = unweighted mean of the available daily means (n_obs not used as a weight)
  - A month counts as missing only if it has zero daily rows; a partly covered month still shows a value
  - The caption's temperature range = warmest minus coldest calendar month, each averaged over all years
limitations:
  - Partly covered months may be biased toward the days that do have readings; the number of days behind each cell is shown on hover
  - The colour scale runs from the lowest to the highest monthly mean in the data, so small differences between neighbouring cells are hard to read exactly
```
